newsitem.title: RUSSIA: One dead, four wounded in Russia Caucasus attack.
newsitem.headline: One dead, four wounded in Russia Caucasus attack.

text.p: One person was killed and four were wounded when gunmen fired a grenade launcher and automatic weapons at a bus carrying quicklime plant workers in the Russian region of North Ossetia, police said on Thursday.

"Shots were fired at the bus from the woods south of the capital Vladikavkaz. The group of attackers was quite large, about 15 people," a duty officer at North Ossetia's Interior Ministry told Reuters by telephone.
All those in the bus were ethnic Ossetians, he said.
He said it was not clear who the attackers were but that there appeared to be a link with the neighbouring region of Ingushetia.

Tensions in the northern Caucasus between Moslem Ingush and Christian North Ossetians have risen in recent weeks, reviving fears that an ancient conflict may flare again. The Kremlin has issued calls for compromise and calm.
Recent clashes have mainly involved Ingush trying to resettle in the Prigorodny district in North Ossetia.
Nearly 200 people were killed in 1992 in fighting over the district, which lies close to the regional capital of Vladikavkaz and used to be inhabited by Ingush.
The Ingush were deported from their land in 1944 by Soviet dictator Josef Stalin and returned in the 1950s to find that some of it, including Prigorodny, was under the jurisdiction of North Ossetia.
Ingushetia and North Ossetia both border Chechnya, where Russian troops fought separatists in a conflict which lasted almost 21 months and ended a year ago.
